title: Is my game AI Slop? 😬
author: PassionateBackfire
selftext:
Recently I got into Godot, coding, and..AI. This was more of a spur of the moment passion project that turned into something genuinely out of hand. Now I'm kinda thinking about going all out with this game just to see what I can do. 

there are many features I forgot to show simply because the footage was actually a playtest and this was not meant to really be a true showcase of the game, but I couldn't take it anymore and had to post it, this game includes full dynamic oil film strength and active engine wear based off horsepower, bore scoring, piston scoring, piston discoloration based off engine tune, torque patterns for bolts, minigames for applying rings, pushing pistons into bores, and using the drill- along with adjustable timing and fully adjustable ECU tuning on the dyno.

AI disclosing >!I was thinking at first like "yknow let people guess just to see" but there is very clearly a reason that I posted this here- so im just going to spill the beans and stop wasting time. Around !<>!This game was made around 90% with AI, including engine block mesh, cylinder head mesh, valvetrain, wear calculations,!<>!essentially all major complex 3d models that make the engines internal componets) customer demand management and RNG, and all animation is also AI, and obviously the really crappy monitors all debugging done by me, All ideas for all in game content are mine, all assets are generated specifically for this game and I use completely free audios that have been checked for fair use.!<

comments.author: soulglider26
comments.body:
It depends

Is this a demo just to see if things are fun? That's always fine. Things don't need to be finished.

Could this be a final product? Not even close. If you released this, it feels like slop, or low effort.

UI, clipping of assests, asset quality, sound quality

But I think you know that

I don't see much point in asking people if your game that's just a 2 week demo is slop unless you planned on this being final (or close to final) quality. Better to ask if people think it seems fun.

replies.author: PassionateBackfire
replies.body: to be fully honest I may have gotten ahead of myself- which im sure is easy to do for beginners doing this kind of stuff- but it is 100% helping me decide what to do next before I go down the wrong rabbit hole and truly reach a point of no return- it was meant to be a demo lol

replies.body:

I made a similar type of post. But I think we have different levels of polish and presentation. Mine wasnt perfect either, but I focused heavily on trying to get close to final quality, then worked a lot on how to showcase it.

replies.author: Stinky_You
replies.body:
I was super hyped when I first had a working piece. I didn't bother with art or the look, that can come close to last or after first slice is near done. Don't skimp on the development plan. Idk what AI you use but claude is very good at coming up with a plan, don't get ahead of Claude and interrogate it (politely) when you don't know or want emphasis. It can also build itself efficiency tools. Pretty much any kind of software I can think of. Crazy times...
Oh yeah my point was it's okay to put all building on hold and strategize with Claude. It's a crazy tool. Also I put my project and dev doc on local storage (my PC) and told Claude to read and edit the entire plan from there and never use the app (huge usage waste)

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: Graphics are clean but generic, nothing wrong with that if it's deep and fun. But you need to get right into the gameplay and what's fun. You made it look super boring. Attention is short, you need to show a core fun gameplay loop within the first 30 seconds or less.
